Yeah, I mean... it definitely started after I took on the condo mortgage. That was, what, about a year and eight months ago now? So this whole thing has been going on for that long. It really kicked off right after I signed those papers.

I actually used to collect pens when I was taking some college classes a while back. I had this whole coffee mug full of them, mostly Pilot G2s, but a couple of fancy fountain pens too. You have to be really careful with fountain pens, though, because the ink gets everywhere if you press too hard, especially on cheap paper. Like, we use this really cheap paper for the order pads at the restaurant, and if you use a wet pen it just bleeds right through to the next ticket and ruins it. The cooks get so mad when they can't read the tickets. But um... yeah, about a year and eight months of feeling like this.\n\nDoctor: If the mortgage problem were somehow resolved, do you think these feelings would mostly go away?\n\nPatient: I don't really know if fixing the mortgage would even matter at this point. Because most days, there’s just this... this heavy, empty feeling sitting right in my chest. It’s like I’m just going through the motions every day, carrying plates and smiling at tables because I’m supposed to, not because I actually feel anything good. \n\nAnd carrying those plates, man, the restaurant just switched to these new stoneware ones that are so incredibly heavy. My manager, Brenda, she insisted on them because she wants the dining room to look more 'farmhouse chic' or whatever. That liquid has to be toxic, right? Like if it got on the host stand or near the silverware. \n\nBut um... sorry, what were you asking? Oh, the mortgage. Yeah, I just feel really empty inside regardless, so I don't think selling the condo would magically fix it.\n\nDoctor: Have you had thoughts of killing yourself?\n\nPatient: Um... well, no, I don't have a specific plan to, like, hurt myself or anything. We use this dark roast from a local roaster, and it's supposed to have these chocolate and cherry notes, but if you mess up the temperature, it just tastes like burnt dirt. Yeah, I guess so. Like at work, I used to joke around with the regulars all the time. I used to text my brother stuff like that all the time after my shifts, just funny videos or whatever happened at work. But now... I don't know, I just let his messages sit there on my phone. I just don't feel the pull to answer him anymore. Even at the restaurant, I mostly just keep my face straight now and say only what I have to say to get the order in. I take the 42, and it always smells like wet wool and old pennies, especially when it rains, and the seats have that weird fuzzy pattern that gives you a headache if you stare at it too long... but yeah, I guess I don't really enjoy the things I used to.
